research_question: In adults, what is the effect of atorvastatin, compared with placebo or no treatment, on withdrawal due to adverse effects?
outcome_description: Withdrawal or discontinuation from the study or assigned treatment because of adverse effects, analyzed as a binary outcome (number of adults withdrawing due to adverse effects out of the number randomized or otherwise included in each comparison group).
positive_direction: A positive effect means atorvastatin is favored because it results in fewer withdrawals due to adverse effects than placebo or no treatment.
search_queries: atorvastatin placebo trial withdrawal adverse effects
atorvastatin controlled study discontinuation adverse events
atorvastatin no treatment comparison adverse effect withdrawal
inclusion_criteria: Original empirical studies in adults that evaluate atorvastatin and include a placebo or no-treatment comparison group.
Studies reporting withdrawal or treatment discontinuation due to adverse effects, or sufficient quantitative information from which this outcome can be derived.
Any treatment duration, atorvastatin dose, clinical indication, care setting, publication status, or language, provided the study is broadly relevant and supplies usable comparative data.
exclusion_criteria: Not an original empirical study, including systematic reviews, meta-analyses, editorials, opinion pieces, and theoretical papers.
No comparison between atorvastatin and a placebo or no-treatment control condition.

No quantitative outcome data that can produce an effect size; for example, no group-specific event counts or proportions, means and standard deviations, t/F-values, or reported odds ratios or other usable comparative estimates.
Completely unrelated to atorvastatin use, adult participants, or withdrawal due to adverse effects.
moderators_to_extract: Participant clinical indication or baseline cardiovascular-risk category
Mean participant age and sex distribution
effect_size_note: Treat withdrawal due to adverse effects as a dichotomous outcome. Extract randomized denominators and event counts by arm preferentially using an intention-to-treat framework; record each study's reported effect estimate when counts are unavailable. Harmonize coding so positive effects favor atorvastatin (fewer withdrawals). For multi-arm studies, avoid double-counting shared controls by combining eligible atorvastatin arms when clinically appropriate or splitting the shared control. Document zero-event handling and assess sensitivity to continuity-correction choices.
